item.title: 3 works of art stolen from France's Renoir Museum, local mayor says
item.description: Authorities in France are seeking two thieves who broke into a museum with the works of Renoir​ and stole "four works of art" but dropped one as they got away, the local mayor said.

item.title: Russian strikes on Kyiv resume as soon as Witkoff, Kushner peace talks end
item.description: Russian strikes pummeled Ukraine's capital as soon as a three-day pause for peace talks with President Trump's envoys ended.

item.title: Small plane goes missing off Bahamas carrying 4 members of Florida family
item.description: A small plane carrying four family members flying back home to Florida went missing off the Bahamas, the U.S. Coast Guard and authorities in the Bahamas said.

item.title: Oil prices up as Iran says it will expand control over Strait of Hormuz
item.description: A top Iranian official says Tehran will impose an "exclusion zone" outside the Strait of Hormuz as it seeks to tighten its chokehold on tanker traffic.

item.title: Canada's retaliatory tariffs on $20 billion in U.S. goods take effect
item.description: Canada's steep retaliatory tariffs on $20 billion in U.S. goods took effect just after midnight ET on Tuesday, deepening the trade war between the two countries.

item.title: State of emergency in Hawaii as Hurricane Lowell approaches
item.description: Hurricane Lowell is barreling toward Hawaii, bringing the potential for life-threatening floods. CBS News' Carter Evans is in Kauai with more. Then, Rob Marciano joins with the latest forecast.

item.title: Amazon cargo plane crash victims were in vehicles that were hit, NTSB says
item.description: An Amazon cargo plane overshot a runway at Miami International Airport and crashed into two vehicles before coming to a stop and bursting into flames. Five people were killed.

item.title: Hurricane warning issued for western Hawaii as Lowell approaches
item.description: The National Hurricane Center posted a hurricane warning for western Hawaii's Kauai County as Hurricane Lowell moved toward the area as a Category 2 storm.

item.title: Accused killers of American and Australian surfers go on trial in Mexico
item.description: Brothers Jake and Callum Robinson and Jack Carter Rhoad were on a surfing trip to Mexico's Pacific coast in April 2024 when they were shot dead in Baja California.

item.title: The science behind making the perfect banana
item.description: There are some unusual jobs out there, but one you've probably never heard of is professional banana ripener. CBS News' Michael George explains what goes into making the perfect banana.

item.title: The nurses who never thought they'd work in healthcare
item.description: Hospitals are looking to hire as a nationwide nursing shortage is expected to worsen in the coming years, and that opportunity is attracting some workers considering a career change. CBS News' Bradley Blackburn reports.

item.title: 25 years after 9/11, Taliban rules Afghanistan again, but with U.S. firepower
item.description: CBS News finds Taliban forces patrolling Kabul in American armored vehicles, wearing American tactical gear and carrying American weapons.

item.title: Mom found guilty of abuse for letting 5-year-old walk outside alone
item.description: "We just expected that as soon as this gets in front of a prosecutor actually looking at it and a judge, this is all gonna go away," Karyann Parkinson said.

item.title: Mom placed on child abuse registry after letting 5-year-old walk alone
item.description: A Virginia mother is walking the line between helping a child develop their independence and criminal child neglect, fighting charges of abuse after letting her 5-year-old son walk outside alone. CBS News' Mark Strassmann is following the story.

item.title: Will Gov. Newsom veto the high-speed rail oversight bill that his own watchdog calls essential?
item.description: Newsom quietly enacted the controversial part of a high-speed rail oversight bill and may now veto the part his watchdog says he needs for transparecy and accountability, sources tell CBS California.

item.title: Secret Elizabeth Holmes documentary debuts at film festival
item.description: Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes, already serving an 11-year sentence for defrauding investors, is now also the star of a new documentary co-created by an absurdist comedian. CBS News' Lilia Luciano has the story.

item.title: King says Prince Harry and Meghan remain private citizens after U.K. return
item.description: Prince Harry and Meghan stepped down as senior working members of the royal family in January 2020, and this position, the letter said, "will continue to be fully respected."

item.title: Prince Harry and Meghan won't be working royals, King Charles confirms
item.description: Prince Harry and Megan Markle have returned to the U.K., but not to any official royal duties. But just in case there is any hint of confusion, King Charles released a letter of clarification on Monday. CBS News' Holly Williams has details.

item.title: Taliban using U.S. weapons 5 years after withdrawal
item.description: The 9/11 terror attacks, 25 years ago this week, were planned from inside the Taliban-controlled country of Afghanistan; a country that tonight is not only back under Taliban control, but with Taliban fighters carrying American weapons and driving around in American vehicles. CBS News' Imtiaz Tyab reports from Kabul.

item.title: Officials investigating cause of deadly Amazon cargo plane crash in Miami
item.description: A federal investigation is underway in Miami after an Amazon cargo plane crashed and hit two vehicles on Sunday, killing five people and injuring five others. CBS News' Skyler Henry reports.

item.title: 9/7: CBS Evening News
item.description: Officials investigating cause of deadly Amazon cargo plane crash in Miami; state of emergency in Hawaii as Hurricane Lowell approaches.

item.title: Pope Leo unveils new fresco at sanctuary where he prayed after his election
item.description: Pope Leo XIV unveiled the portrait before celebrating Mass with his fellow Augustinian brothers at the Sanctuary of Our Mother of Good Counsel​ in the medieval village of Genazzano, south of Rome.

item.title: Kushner attributes the lack of progress on Gaza to upcoming Israeli elections
item.description: U.S. efforts to advance plans​ to disarm Hamas and open the way for investment into rebuilding Gaza have stalled.

item.title: Witness says seeing Amazon plane crash at MIA was "something from a movie"
item.description: Five people were killed and five others were injured when a plane overshot a runway at Miami International Airport and crashed.

item.title: Drone activity at border drops 75% after U.S. uses laser weapon, military says
item.description: In less than two weeks, the high-energy laser weapon system has taken down 11 drones, coinciding with a 75% drop in drones probing the border, military officials told CBS News.

item.title: What's open and closed on Labor Day 2026? See which businesses are operating.
item.description: Most major retail stores and grocery chains will remain open on Labor Day, while banks will close.

item.title: 9/6/2026: Sharswood; Boom Chicago
item.description: First, man unknowingly buys former plantation house where his ancestors were enslaved. Then, a look at the Amsterdam improv club behind comedy legends.

item.title: Passenger duct taped to seat after allegedly calling flight attendant racial slur
item.description: A passenger on an American Airlines flight was duct-taped to a seat after he allegedly used a racial slur against a flight attendant and punched a fellow passenger.

item.title: Work on Trump-backed triumphal arch will start in coming weeks
item.description: The federal government plans to start excavation over the next two weeks on a massive triumphal arch near Washington, D.C., Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum said, a controversial project championed by President Trump.

item.title: Artemis crew tells kids moon flight was "the best roller coaster ride"
item.description: The Artemis II astronauts joined "CBS Mornings" for a live town hall where they took questions from kids just weeks after returning from their historic moon mission.
